name: Vue Shapeshifter Table
tagline: A table that adapts to your application.

pages.title: Introduction
pages.lead: A table that adapts to your application.

blocks.text: A reusable Vue 3 component library by Saqif Hoque. Install the package in your own application, connect your data, and shape the surrounding interface however you need.

items: Real component, not an iframe or a hosted service.
ES module package, styles, and public TypeScript declarations.
Live examples use the published npm package, not a source-code alias.

blocks.text: npm install vue-shapeshifter-table vue@^3.3.0
Use the navigation to get started, open the playground, or look up individual props. These docs cover npm version 1.1.1.

pages.title: Installation
pages.lead: Add the package to an existing Vue 3 application.

blocks.text: npm install vue-shapeshifter-table "vue@^3.3.0"
Import the component and its CSS once in your application. Vue is a peer dependency; keep a single compatible Vue instance.

import { ShapeShifterTable } from 'vue-shapeshifter-table'
import 'vue-shapeshifter-table/style.css'
The default export is also a Vue plugin. Named component imports are convenient for local registration. No backend is required by the component.

pages.title: Quick start
pages.lead: Render the component inside an ordinary div.

blocks.text: The div belongs to your application. You control its dimensions, layout, and other UI. The imported package renders the interactive component inside it.
Each column has a stable key. Each row is an array of cell objects; cell content lives in field.

pages.title: Live playground
pages.lead: Try the published component and inspect its integration code.

blocks.text: This is a real npm consumer, running in your browser. Changes here are demonstration state and reset when you reload.

pages.title: Props
pages.lead: Public component inputs from the installed npm TypeScript declarations.

head: Prop
Type
Purpose
rows: Controlled sort state: { key, direction } or null.
Column definitions with unique stable keys. Bind with v-model:headers.
Rows represented as arrays of cell objects. Bind with v-model:table-data.
Optional small text above the table heading.
Message shown when the table has no rows.
Keep the header visible while scrolling.
Allow rows and columns to be added.
Allow rows and columns to be removed.
Enable pointer and keyboard column reordering.

blocks.text: Use kebab-case in templates: tableData becomes table-data. Optional features such as sorting, filtering, pagination, and dragging are off until enabled.

pages.title: Data model & editing
pages.lead: Understand headers, cells, and change events.

blocks.text:
const headers = ref([{ key: 'name', field: 'Name' }])
const rows = ref([[{ field: 'Amina', key: 'user-1' }]])

items: Header keys must be unique stable strings or finite numbers.
Rows are arrays in the same column order as headers. Each cell is an object with a field value.
Bind both headers and table-data so edits and structural changes remain in your application state.
Cell edits normally produce strings; narrow or convert values before sending them to your API.
Row indices in edit/delete events refer to the complete source dataset, including when paginated.

blocks.text:
<ShapeShifterTable v-model:headers="headers"
  v-model:table-data="rows" @cell-update="saveCell" />
The component emits changes; your application owns server persistence. The component does not automatically save table values.

pages.title: Sorting & search
pages.lead: Turn large local datasets into a useful table.

items: Sort buttons cycle ascending → descending → original order.
Finite numbers sort numerically; other supported values use natural text order.
Search uses a trimmed, case-insensitive substring across supported cell values.
The view applies filtering, then sorting, then pagination without reordering the parent row array.

blocks.text: These operations run in the browser over the full supplied dataset. This is not a server-side query or virtualization API. Custom comparators and per-column filters on GitHub are not part of this 1.1.1 reference.

pages.title: Pagination
pages.lead: Display a page of your rows while retaining the full dataset.

blocks.text:
<ShapeShifterTable v-model:headers="headers"
  v-model:table-data="rows" pagination
  v-model:page="page" v-model:page-size="pageSize"
  :page-size-options="[10, 25, 50]" />

head: Input
Behavior
rows: Sorting and search return the view to page 1.
Page is clamped to the available range.

blocks.text: Paging is opt-in. Every row remains in memory. Draft editing ends when navigating between pages.

pages.title: Column order & persistence
pages.lead: Move columns and restore a saved layout.

blocks.text:
<ShapeShifterTable v-model:headers="headers"
  v-model:table-data="rows" draggable-columns />
Drag a handle or focus it and use the arrow keys. Reordering moves headers and matching cells across all rows, including rows hidden by pagination.
Wrap browser storage reads and writes in try/catch. Stale, duplicate, and unknown saved keys are tolerated; new schema columns are appended. SSR applications should access storage after mounting.

pages.title: Slots
pages.lead: Use your own cell, header, toolbar, and empty-state UI.

blocks.text: A custom cell slot replaces the default cell presentation. Provide your own editor when using custom interactive cells. Short rows may contain undefined cells.

pages.title: Events
pages.lead: Observe mutations or control view state.

pages.title: TypeScript & SSR
pages.lead: Typed component bindings without a separate @types package.

blocks.text: Use Vue 3.3+ and TypeScript 5+ with Bundler or NodeNext module resolution. Cell fields are unknown; narrow them before formatting or using them as a domain type.
Registering the default plugin works at runtime. Import the named component in typed Vue SFCs for template inference. Read and write localStorage only after mounting in SSR applications.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.lead: Check data bindings, styles, and client-side behavior.

head: Symptom
Check
rows: Bind both models with v-model; the application owns its state.
Keep header keys unique and update headers and rows together.
Editors produce strings; convert values in your application.
Sorting, filtering, and pagination are client-side; limit the dataset or implement a different server-backed view.
Use compatible Vue/TypeScript versions and Bundler or NodeNext resolution.

pages.title: License & package contents
pages.lead: Keep the component small and your demo separate.

blocks.text: Vue Shapeshifter Table is MIT licensed. Preserve its copyright and license notice when redistributing it.

The npm package contains the compiled library, CSS, TypeScript declarations, and documentation. The demo application, sample data, and docs website remain in GitHub and are not installed with the library.
The playground uses fictional data stored in memory. Only the explicit Save column order action writes the layout keys to browser storage.
